groups.text: It is currently 17 degrees and mostly clear in Berlin-Tempelhof.
With the morning weather set, here is the news.

Many AI coding tools assume a single model should handle every task, from understanding the initial request to writing and reviewing the final code. To challenge this approach, a developer has built an open source pipeline called AutoDev Studio that allows different models to manage each stage of the software development lifecycle. This system enables users to mix local LLMs with hosted models, such as using DeepSeek-R1 for planning and Claude Code for implementation. By ensuring the reviewer is always from a different model family than the author, the system prevents a model from approving its own work. In separate technical news, PyTorch has released incremental updates to switch the default for the NCCL backend. This update adds an explicit legacy backend entry point that creates the existing ProcessGroupNCCL, allowing developers to test existing implementations independently as they move toward new defaults.

In Ukraine, Russian guided bombs struck a residential area in Sumy overnight, injuring three adults and three children. Oleh Hryhorov, head of the Sumy Regional Military Administration, reports that private houses were destroyed or damaged, though there were no fatalities. In Nedryhailiv, a drone attack on civilian infrastructure also caused casualties. Elsewhere in Europe, French communes in Meuse and Ardennes are struggling with record levels of Pfas pollution. For over a year, drinking tap water has been banned in about twenty towns as similar alerts regarding these forever chemicals multiply across France. Local officials face astronomical costs and logistical hurdles that make permanent cleanup solutions difficult to implement. Meanwhile, in India, researchers have discovered a new species of trapdoor spider, Tigidia singhal, in the semi-arid grasslands of Maharashtra. Found during a vegetation survey on the Deccan Plateau, this discovery expands the known range of the genus into open natural ecosystems.

In India, the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan has sparked celebrations at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi. The "Cockroach Janta Party" led these protests for 36 days after leaked exam papers forced over two million students to repeat their university entrance tests, a crisis that drove some students to suicide. Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government is now offering maximum compensation to the families of those students. Meanwhile, in France, Orange is forming a joint venture with New Zealand's Morrison to increase its data center capacity tenfold to 400 megawatts. This partnership leverages Morrison's capital to build new facilities across four French campuses, supporting AI and cloud solutions for professional clients. In a separate matter in Ukraine, the Kyiv city military recruitment center confirmed that Hromadske journalist Yevhen Shulhat was detained and subsequently released with a summons to undergo a medical commission.

In Berlin, people are laying flowers near the site of a suspected Islamist attack on the Christopher Street Day parade. The suspect, Abdul B., was already a convicted criminal under observation by security authorities, leading to questions about why he remained free and whether youth sentencing laws should apply to adult offenders who pose a danger. Meanwhile, in Adelaide, factional powerbrokers at the Labor Party’s 50th national conference worked to suppress discussions on contentious issues, including the war in Gaza and the AUKUS pact. These leaders aimed to present a united front to the ruling class despite mass anti-war demonstrations across Australia. In a different sphere of public safety, France 24 reports that food-related health warnings are becoming so frequent that avoiding contaminants like cadmium and forever chemicals now seems nearly impossible for the average consumer.

Apple is accelerating its security update cycle to counter generative AI, which the company says allows for the rapid development of malicious hacking tools. This shift is evident in the latest releases of iOS 26.6 and macOS 26.6 Tahoe, which patch 87 and 155 vulnerabilities respectively. While no zero-day exploits were active before these fixes, several flaws are considered very serious, including a vulnerability in the AVEVideoEncoder component that could allow an application to execute arbitrary code with kernel privileges. In contrast to these preventative measures, Australian power company Origin Energy is dealing with a successful breach affecting 900,000 current and former customers. Threat actors accessed names, addresses, and partial payment details, while one individual claimed to have stolen data from two million customers. CEO Frank Calabria stated the matter is now a criminal investigation by relevant authorities.

The world risks a resurgence of the HIV epidemic as global funding fell eighteen percent to seven point three billion dollars last year. UNAIDS reports this is the lowest funding level in nearly two decades, threatening progress that had driven new infections and deaths to their lowest levels in over thirty years. Washington previously provided seventy-five percent of international HIV funding before President Donald Trump returned to office in January 2025 and ordered a temporary halt to those funds. In other news, MAGA influencer Laura Loomer now admits she was wrong to claim Ukraine started the war, stating she fell victim to Russian propaganda. After visiting Kyiv and frontline communities, Loomer now argues that a Ukrainian victory serves American national interests. Meanwhile, a fifty-one-year-old New Zealand woman flew nine thousand kilometers to Hanoi for a hip replacement at Viet Duc University Hospital after waiting four years for the procedure at home.

The occupied West Bank is gripped by arson, raids, and road closures following a deadly attack southwest of Nablus. More than 20 Israeli settlers from the Havat Gilad settlement attacked homes in Tal on July 24; videos show a Palestinian man shooting a settler dead before soldiers shot the man dead. Four members of the Ramadan family were killed in the violence, along with an Israeli soldier and a settler. In France, local authorities say a megafire near Bordeaux remained stable Tuesday morning after burning 42,000 hectares since July 22, though rising temperatures may reignite the blaze. Meanwhile, Prime Minister Andy Burnham has outlined reforms to bring technical subjects like AI and manufacturing into English secondary schools starting in Year 10. The government aims to create clearer pathways to work for the more than one million young people currently not in education, employment, or training.
After the headlines, back to the weather.
This afternoon will be cloudy with temperatures between 20 and 25 degrees.
And from the weather, a quick look at the calendar.

On your calendar today: Your work calendar has weekly lunch at noon, NAS sync at two in the afternoon, and a RAYX meeting at three. Your personal calendar has summer holidays in Berlin all day, followed by Krebs at six in the evening.
Mail worth checking: You have a few messages from Kleinanzeigen regarding your listings and two shipping notifications from Amazon about packages arriving tomorrow.
And that's it for your personal morning broadcast.
[mature adult voice, intensely emotional, tender, radiant; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
[very very long pause before speaking; then mature adult voice, most emotional, strong, warm, radiant, deeply encouraging; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
